about: Every data op, at every place in a message it can name, in each direction: whether the compiler serves it, or blocks the release and why. A test builds a Change for every cell and checks the compiler does what the cell says, and fails if any cell is missing. Endpoint ops (route, retire, behavior) act on a whole operation and are listed once each.

body request.why: A schema scope reaches every request body that uses the schema.

body response.why: A schema scope reaches every response body that uses the schema, undone in reverse.

query request.why: The gate blocks: only schema scopes are served until the request envelope (M3.4).

path request.why: The gate blocks: only schema scopes are served until the request envelope (M3.4).

header request.why: The gate blocks: only schema scopes are served until the request envelope (M3.4).

header response.why: The IR has no scope for response headers yet; the request envelope adds one (M3.4).

route.why: The runtime routes an old caller's method and path to the new ones.

retire.why: The runtime answers 410 with the provider's guidance, and the provider never sees the call.

behavior.why: The runtime exposes the flag, and the provider branches on it in its own code.
